Boat electrical repair: batteries, charging, wiring, bilge pumps, corrosion

Dead batteries every morning, gauges that drop out, nav lights that work when they feel like it, a bilge pump that doesn't. Marine electrical specialists trace it properly instead of swapping parts.

What's included

  • Battery load test and charging system test
  • Parasitic draw diagnosis
  • Switch panel, breakers, and wiring repair
  • Bilge pump and float switch replacement
  • Nav and courtesy lighting
  • Battery switch and ACR/isolator setup
  • Shore power and charger faults
  • Corroded grounds and connections
When

Intermittent anything, dead batteries, burning smell, breakers that trip, before adding electronics or a trolling motor.

Time on site

1 to 4 hours

What it usually costs here

$150 to $700 for most diagnostics and repairs; battery replacements add $150 to $400 per battery; rewiring projects quoted.

In Tampa Bay specifically

Salt air corrodes grounds first. Boats kept on lifts in Dunedin, Tarpon Springs, and Apollo Beach canals show ground corrosion long before anything else fails.

Engines

YamahaMercurySuzukiHonda MarineMerCruiser

Questions we get

Why do my batteries die overnight?

A parasitic draw (stereo memory, bilge pump cycling, a bad charger), a battery past its life, or a switch left on. A draw test with a clamp meter finds it in under an hour.

Lithium house batteries?

Yes, with the charger and alternator protection to match. The mechanic will say if your setup needs a DC-DC charger.
